title: The last days, alone
hookLine: read the last chapter of DN 16
tomorrow: a young man bows to six directions every morning. why?

cards: The last day of a class with a teacher you'll miss has its own quiet. The bell is about to ring, and everybody waits for the one sentence. DN 16 ends that way, between two trees near Kusinara.
The Buddha is dying, and the monks have gathered. Ananda is grieving: soon we'll have no teacher. And what he leaves them with is not a successor, and not a relic.

teach.h: THE TEACHING WILL BE YOUR TEACHER.
teach.b: Today's question: what does a teacher leave behind? First, the Buddha tells Ananda, in paraphrase: don't think you have no teacher. The teaching and the discipline I gave you will be your teacher when I'm gone.
Then he asks the monks, three times, if anyone has a doubt left.
Silence. And then, in the old Rhys Davids English: "Decay is inherent in all component things! Work out your salvation with diligence!" Everything made comes apart; strive on.
A neighbor tradition has a farewell that sounds close.

teach.h: PAUL: WORK OUT YOUR OWN SALVATION.
teach.b: Paul, writing to the Christians at Philippi, tells them to keep going in his absence: "work out your own salvation with fear and trembling."

Notice those words, work out your salvation, in both old English versions. That's what they share: a teacher stepping away and handing the work to the students, trusting them to continue without him in the room.
And the honest difference: Paul's next line says it is God who works in them.

The Buddha's last words put the weight on the students' own diligence, with the teaching as their teacher. Even within Buddhism, Shinran leaned on a power beyond the self. Different roads, each described in its own words.

how: The Buddha's passing (parinibbana) is remembered on festival days such as Vesak in some traditions and Nirvana Day in others, and his last words are recited and taught as a summary of the path.

s: the Buddha named a successor to lead after him
he told Ananda the teaching and discipline would be their teacher.
the old English 'work out your salvation' also appears in a letter of Paul
Philippians 2:12, 'work out your own salvation with fear and trembling.'
Paul and the Buddha say exactly the same thing
both hand the work to their students; Paul adds that God works in them, while the Buddha points to their own diligence.

games.q: your piano teacher is moving away. she says, 'you have everything you need.' what would DN 16 have you do?
o: keep practicing what she taught; the teaching is now your teacher
stop until you find someone exactly like her
take a break, since the lessons are officially over
games.why: the Buddha told the grieving monks the teaching would be their teacher, then said: strive on. a farewell is a handoff, not an ending.

practice: Sit in silence, the way the monks did after his question. No technique, no counting. Just stay present and awake, as if someone had asked whether you have a doubt left, and you're listening for the answer.

wordCard.voice: The last days: DN 16, the Buddha's final journey, ending with the teaching as teacher and one last word: strive on.

orig.note: Pali: heedfulness, diligence, not being careless. The last word of DN 16 is built on it.

carryVoice: Strive on: the teacher goes, and the teaching stays right here in your hands. Until tomorrow.
